summary_paragraph: A male patient was admitted 30 days after a deceased donor pediatric en bloc kidney transplant for nausea, vomiting, and constipation. He had not passed stool or gas in three days, though his graft function remained stable with a creatinine of 1.2–1.4. Imaging confirmed moderate fecal loading without obstruction and showed an interval increase in pelvic fullness of both transplanted kidneys with a stable complex perinephric fluid collection. Constipation was managed with milk of magnesia, enemas, and lactulose, leading to resolution. His Prograf level was initially elevated at 16.6, prompting a dose reduction to 3 mg twice daily, with subsequent improvement to 11.2. Due to low white blood cell count, Valcyte was reduced, and antihypertensives were adjusted for low blood pressure. The wound VAC was discontinued as the incision healed. He was discharged home with home health support on adjusted immunosuppression, continued micafungin, and instructions for ongoing monitoring.
